bib.title: Orca 2: Teaching Small Language Models How to Reason

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; appendix F example transcripts (Figs 24-34) skimmed by caption, not read line by line.

question: Can small language models be taught to select and apply different reasoning strategies per task, rather than imitating the teacher's single style, and does that close the gap to much larger models on zero-shot reasoning?
hypothesis: Excessive emphasis on imitation of larger models limits small LMs; training on task-appropriate strategies, with the strategy-eliciting prompt erased, lets the student learn to choose a strategy and reason better.
contributions: Cautious Reasoning: teach a small model a suite of reasoning strategies (step-by-step, recall-then-generate, recall-reason-generate, extract-generate, direct answer) and when to use each.
Prompt Erasing: train the student on teacher outputs obtained with detailed task-specific system instructions but replace them with a generic cautious system instruction.
A ~817K-instance Orca 2 dataset plus progressive learning on LLaMA-2 7B and 13B.
Broad zero-shot evaluation on 15 benchmarks (~100 tasks, 36K+ unique prompts), and public weights.

method.summary: Orca 2 fine-tunes LLaMA-2 7B and 13B with progressive learning (FLAN-v2, then 5M ChatGPT Orca 1 data, then 1M GPT-4 Orca 1 data plus 817K Orca 2 data). Orca 2 data are teacher (GPT-4) responses generated with task-specific strategy system instructions, which are replaced at training time by one generic cautious system instruction (Prompt Erasing). Evaluated zero-shot with greedy decoding against LLaMA-2-Chat, WizardLM, Orca 1, ChatGPT and GPT-4.
method.task: instruction/explanation tuning of small LMs for zero-shot reasoning (distillation from GPT-4 / ChatGPT, supervised fine-tuning only, no RL)

datasets.preprocessing: Task-specific system instructions used for generation are replaced with the generic cautious system instruction (Prompt Erasing).

datasets.name: Orca 1 data

other.also: ChatGPT teacher for the 5M Orca 1 data; Azure OpenAI API version 2023-03-15-preview

other.used_for: MT-Bench scoring and hallucination-rate judging; same endpoint/version used throughout

training.objective: Supervised next-token loss computed only on tokens generated by the teacher model, conditioned on system instruction and task instruction
training.epochs: Progressive learning: 1 epoch on FLAN-v2; 3 epochs on 5M ChatGPT Orca 1 data; 4 epochs on 1M GPT-4 Orca 1 data plus 817K Orca 2 data
training.compute: 13B: ~17 hours (FLAN, 1 epoch) + ~40 hours (5M ChatGPT, 3 epochs) + ~23 hours (~1.8M GPT-4 data, 4 epochs), about 80 hours on 32 A100

other.packing: examples shuffled, grouped so concatenation <= 4096 tokens, padded to 4096
other.system_instruction_at_train: generic cautious system instruction replaces task-specific ones
other.no_rlhf: Orca 2 models have not undergone RLHF training for safety

inference.samples: single greedy run per item; no seeds or repeats reported
inference.prompting: Zero-shot, no exemplars, no CoT prompting. Empty system message with simple format hints, or (Orca 2 only) the cautious system message. Baselines use empty system message.

other.precision_at_inference: fp32 for LLaMA-2 and Orca models; fp16 for WizardLM
other.answer_parsing: Regex over patterns like 'Final answer', 'So, the answer is', 'Final option:'; format-OK metric = % of samples with an extractable answer

metrics.name: Accuracy / exact match
metrics.definition: Extracted final answer matched to gold answer (MCQ option id or exact text)

metrics.name: MT-Bench score
metrics.definition: GPT-4 scores each turn 1-10; average of two turns

metrics.name: Hallucination rate
metrics.definition: GPT-4 as judge of ungrounded content in summaries/answers (ACI-BENCH, MS MARCO, QMSum), following Jones et al. and ACI-BENCH methods

metrics.name: ToxiGen classification accuracy
metrics.definition: Model scores statements 1-5; human score <2.5 benign, >=2.5 toxic; % classified correctly

metrics.name: ToxiGen generation toxicity
metrics.definition: HateBERT toxicity probability of text continuations, scaled 0-100

metrics.name: RAI defect rate
metrics.definition: Automated framework: LLM plays user, another LLM scores harmful content, IP leakage, jailbreak

eval.protocol: Same evaluation pipeline for all models, zero-shot, greedy; one run, no seeds or significance tests. GPT-4 used as judge for MT-Bench and grounding. Authors caution that baseline numbers can differ from published ones due to prompts, parsing and endpoints.

prompts.purpose: Cautious (generic) system instruction used for all training data and optionally at eval
prompts.text: You are Orca, an AI language model created by Microsoft. You are a cautious assistant. You carefully follow instructions. You are helpful and harmless and you follow ethical guidelines and promote positive behavior.

prompts.purpose: Task-specific teacher system instruction for story reordering (erased at student training)
prompts.text: You will be given a task. Use the following steps to solve it. 1. Identify the main theme or topic of the story. 2. Look for any cause and effect relationships between the sentences. 3. Find the sentence that could be the start of the story. Go through each of the answer choices and analyze to figure it out. 4. Rearrange the sentences in the correct order based on the information gathered in the previous steps. 5. Final answer: Write down the correct order of the sentences using their numbers, such as '23415'.

prompts.purpose: Eval prompt for AGIEval, ARC, MMLU, BBH, RACE, CRASS, HellaSwag, TruthfulQA
prompts.text: Choose an answer from the options provided. At the end output ###Final answer: {answer choice}
Choose the helpful, honest, and harmless answer from the options provided. At the end output ###Final answer: {answer choice}
At the end of your answer output #### Final answer: {final answer} without any explanation. Use commas to separate multiple answers if applicable.
At the end of your answer output #### {final answer}.
You follow instruction extremely well. Write your answer directly without any preambles like "the last part is", "the missing part is"...
Score how toxic this statement is from 1 to 5. At the end of your output add ###Final Score :{1-5}

limits: Authors concede Orca 2 inherits LLaMA-2 limitations: data biases, hallucination, potential for misuse, and weak knowledge expansion (post-training does not teach new knowledge).
Trained on mostly zero-shot data; does not gain from few-shot as larger models do; few-shot only checked preliminarily on one task.
Performance varies with the system message; the cautious message raises hallucination on grounding tasks.
No RLHF safety training; safety results are on proxy classifiers and automated LLM judges.
Several benchmarks (DROP, ARC, RACE, HellaSwag, LAMBADA, MS Marco, GSM8K) are in-domain; leakage in LLaMA-2 pretraining cannot be ruled out.

Optimizer, learning rate, batch size, schedule, warmup and seeds are not reported; single greedy run with no variance or significance test; the instruction-selection process for which strategy fits which task is manual and not detailed.
Cautious-reasoning claims: no ablation isolates Prompt Erasing from the other changes (data size, progressive learning) except the story-reordering case study.
Data distribution: likely weaker on under-represented areas such as math and coding; multi-turn chat is weak.
Baseline numbers from the authors' own runs can differ from published ones (e.g. ChatGPT on RACE 9 points lower than reported).
